questions.prompt: The probability that a single normal measurement exceeds 50 is $p = 0.30$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the probability that in 3 independent measurements, all three measurements exceed 50.

questions.prompt: For a continuous random variable $X$, the probability that an observation is less than 12 is $P(X < 12) = 0.15$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: In a random sample of 4 independent observations of $X$, find the probability that none of the observations are less than 12.

questions.prompt: A manufactured component is classified as Grade A with probability $p = 0.6915$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the probability that in a random selection of 4 independent components, exactly 2 components are Grade A.

questions.prompt: In an environmental testing station, the probability of exceeding a safe emission limit on any given day is $p = 0.20$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Over a period of 5 independent days, find the probability that the safe emission limit is exceeded on fewer than 2 days.

questions.prompt: Independent measurements $X_A$ and $X_B$ are taken from two different manufacturing processes, where $P(X_A < 46) = 0.0668$ and $P(X_B < 46) = 0.6732$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the probability that both measurements are less than 46.

questions.prompt: A measurement from a normal distribution lies within $1.5$ standard deviations of the mean with probability $0.8664$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the probability that each of 3 independently chosen measurements lies within $1.5$ standard deviations of the mean.

questions.prompt: The masses $X$ grams of food packets are normally distributed with mean $60.0\text{ g}$ and standard deviation $8.0\text{ g}$, so that $X \sim \text{N}(60.0, 8.0^2)$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the probability that a randomly chosen packet has mass less than $68.0\text{ g}$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Three packets are selected independently at random. Find the probability that all three packets have mass less than $68.0\text{ g}$.

questions.prompt: Apples harvested from an orchard are graded by size. The probability that a randomly selected apple is graded as Medium is $p = 0.692$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Four apples are chosen independently at random. Find the probability that none of the four apples are graded as Medium.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Four apples are chosen independently at random. Find the probability that at least 2 of the apples are graded as Medium.

questions.prompt: The daily usage time $U$ hours of a network server is normally distributed with mean $8.0\text{ hours}$ and standard deviation $1.25\text{ hours}$, so that $U \sim \text{N}(8.0, 1.25^2)$. A day is designated as Heavy Use if the usage time exceeds $9.0\text{ hours}$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the probability that a randomly chosen day is designated as Heavy Use.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Over a period of 10 independent days, find the probability that there are fewer than 2 Heavy Use days.

questions.prompt: The processing time $T$ minutes for loan applications follows the normal distribution $T \sim \text{N}(45, 8^2)$. An application is considered Delayed if it takes more than 57 minutes to process.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Show that the probability that a randomly chosen application is Delayed is $0.0668$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A random sample of $n$ applications is selected independently. Find the smallest value of $n$ such that the probability of finding at least one Delayed application is greater than $0.90$.

questions.prompt: The commute times $X$ minutes for office workers are normally distributed with mean $50\text{ minutes}$ and standard deviation $10\text{ minutes}$, so that $X \sim \text{N}(50, 10^2)$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the probability that a randomly chosen commute time lies between 40 and 65 minutes.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Four commute times are selected independently at random. Calculate the probability that all four commute times lie between 40 and 65 minutes, and find the probability that exactly 3 of the four commute times lie between 40 and 65 minutes.

questions.prompt: The capacity $C\text{ mAh}$ of lithium battery cells follows the normal distribution $C \sim \text{N}(3200, 80^2)$. A cell is classified as High Capacity if its capacity exceeds $3300\text{ mAh}$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the probability that a randomly chosen cell is classified as High Capacity.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: In a pack of 6 independent cells, find the probability that at least 2 cells are classified as High Capacity, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the smallest number of cells $n$ that must be tested so that the probability of finding at least one High Capacity cell is greater than $0.98$.

questions.prompt:
A construction company sources steel bolts from two suppliers. Shear strengths $S\text{ kN}$ of bolts follow independent normal distributions:
- Supplier 1: $S_1 \sim \text{N}(40.0, 2.5^2)$
- Supplier 2: $S_2 \sim \text{N}(42.0, 3.0^2)$
A bolt is rated Extra Strong if its shear strength exceeds $45.0\text{ kN}$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the probability that a randomly chosen bolt from Supplier 1 is Extra Strong, and find the probability that a randomly chosen bolt from Supplier 2 is Extra Strong.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: One bolt from Supplier 1 and one bolt from Supplier 2 are chosen independently at random. Calculate the probability that both bolts are Extra Strong, and calculate the probability that exactly one of the two bolts is Extra Strong.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: A random sample of 5 bolts is selected independently from Supplier 2. Find the probability that fewer than 2 of the bolts are Extra Strong, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
